Hmm, `@Testcontainers` on abstract superclass: JUnit extension finds @Container fields in superclass? Usually yes, and static containers are shared JVM-wide, restarted once stopped. Testcontainers stops static containers after all tests in the class... Actually static containers are started once and stopped at JVM shutdown (Ryuk), not after each class. But `@Testcontainers` extension stops containers after each test class that declares them? No — the extension stops them in `afterAll` only if... Let me recall: `TestcontainersExtension` afterAll → `stopContainers` for containers whose lifecycle is PER_CLASS? For static containers, it stops them at the end of the class by default (unless reusable). Yes, TestcontainersExtension.afterAll stops all containers declared in the class (including inherited static). So each test class restart... but should restart them for the next class since each class gets fresh start. Hmm but connection refused to localhost:57969 means the new class used old port? The Spring context cached — same context reused across test classes? With different `@MockitoBean` sets, contexts differ, but EmailVerificationLimitsIT and TeacherInviteIT both have MailService mock... Contexts: ApprovalAccessIT has no mock, so context A; EmailVerificationLimitsIT context B; RegistrationFlowIT context B; TeacherInviteIT context B... Fix: use singleton container pattern — start containers once in static initializer without `@Testcontainers`/`@Container` management, so they're never stopped between classes (Ryuk cleans up at JVM exit). Standard Spring Boot docs pattern:

```java
static PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>("postgres:17-alpine");
static GenericContainer<?> redis = ...;
static {
    postgres.start();
    redis.start();
}
```

Hmm, but in Boot docs example they use static @Container and no issue because single test class usually. There's a known issue where multiple test classes with differing context configs cause this.
